summary: This standards-track document defines a vendor-specific protocol on the TRILL RBridge Channel. The RBridge Channel is a general mechanism for sending typed messages between RBridges. This lets vendors carry their own messages over it.

plainLanguage.summary: A shared mailroom lets companies drop in notes of their own with their company stamp. Vendors can send private notes between TRILL switches.

subtitle: A slot in the TRILL RBridge Channel where a vendor can send its own messages, identified by its OUI or CID.

tldr.problem: Vendors of TRILL switches may want to send their own diagnostic or control messages between RBridges, or between an RBridge and an end station, without waiting for an RFC.
tldr.mechanism: The Vendor-Specific RBridge Channel Protocol (channel protocol 0x008) puts the vendor's OUI or CID, an error byte and optional sub-protocol and sub-version bytes at the start of the payload, and leaves the rest to the vendor.
tldr.outcome: IETF-defined error codes 1 to 4 cover truncated messages and unknown vendor, sub-protocol or sub-version. The protocol itself gives no security, so any needed security must come from the vendor's own data.

today: RFC 8381 is a Proposed Standard published in May 2018. The metadata shows no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
TRILL switches, also called RBridges, can exchange typed messages using the RBridge Channel facility from RFC 7178. This document specifies a method of sending messages defined by a particular organization over that facility, identified by an OUI (Organizationally Unique Identifier) or a CID (Company Identifier). Such messages could, for example, be vendor-specific diagnostic or control messages.

The RFC adds a nudge: a range of RBridge Channel protocol numbers is available based on RFC publication, and those intending to use the facility are encouraged to document their use in an RFC and use those numbers instead.
sections.plainLanguage: Companies get their own corner of the shared mailroom for private notes, but the mailroom would rather you wrote your rules down publicly if you can.

sections.title: The Vendor Channel Packet
sections.content:
An RBridge Channel packet between RBridges has a link header, a TRILL header, inner Ethernet addresses, a data label (VLAN or FGL), an RBridge Channel header, a channel-protocol-specific payload and a link trailer. When a message goes between an RBridge and an end station on the same link, it is a Native RBridge Channel message and the TRILL header, inner addresses and data label are omitted. The Ethertype for RBridge Channel is 0x8946, and the Protocol field says how to read the payload.

For the vendor protocol, the Channel Protocol value is 0x008. The payload starts with a Vendor ID holding the OUI or CID, and the vendor named there is in charge of specifying the messages. If the bottom two bits of the first byte are 00 the ID is an OUI; if they are 10 it is a CID. Any other value is invalid and a VERR of 2 MUST be returned, subject to possible rate limiting.

After the Vendor ID come the VERR error byte, a Sub-Protocol byte and a Sub-Version byte, then the vendor's own data. Vendors can do whatever they want with the bits after VERR, but it is strongly RECOMMENDED that they use the sub-protocol and sub-version fields so multiple and evolving uses can share one OUI.
sections.plainLanguage: Each note starts with the company stamp, then a space for "something went wrong", then a topic number and a version number. Everything after that is the company's own business.

sections.title: Vendor Channel Errors
sections.content:
VERR values 0x0 through 0x0F and 0xFF are reserved for the IETF. All other values are available for vendor use, except that an implementation MUST NOT send a Vendor Channel Error in response to a message with a nonzero VERR, which prevents error replies about error replies.

  • 0: no error; VERR is zero unless the packet is reporting an error.
  • 1: the data is shorter than 4 bytes, so the VERR byte and possibly part of the OUI is truncated. The receiver MUST extend the message through the VERR field, set it to one and return it.
  • 2: unknown OUI/CID. If the VERR is zero, the OUI/CID is not recognized and the SL flag is zero, the receiver MUST set VERR to two and return it.
  • 3: unknown Sub-Protocol, for a recognized OUI/CID with zero VERR and zero SL flag. An RBridge SHOULD return it.
  • 4: unknown Sub-Version, for a recognized OUI/CID and Sub-Protocol under the same conditions. An RBridge SHOULD return it.

Errors 3 and 4 are only SHOULD because, as long as messages are distinguished by the vendor's OUI/CID, the vendor can decide between standard and nonstandard error handling.
sections.plainLanguage: If a note is cut off, from an unknown company, or about a topic or version you do not know, you send it back marked with a number saying why. You never send back a note that is already an error report.

sections.title: Sending an Error Response
sections.content:
An error response is the received packet, modified, with the VERR field set and the SL flag set in the RBridge Channel Header. The ERR field will be zero, because a nonzero ERR would have been handled at the general RBridge Channel level. For error 1, the data area is extended to include the VERR byte.

  • Between RBridges: clear the M bit, set the egress nickname to the received ingress nickname, set the ingress nickname to one held by the sending TRILL switch, and set the hop count to the usual value for that switch.
  • Between an RBridge and an end station: set Outer.MacDA to the received Outer.MacSA and set Outer.MacSA to the MAC address of the sending port.
  • The priority MAY be reduced (unless already minimum), the Drop Eligibility Indicator bit MAY be set, and error responses MAY be rate-limited.

The whole offending packet is generally expected to be sent back as the payload so responses are easy to match, though except for errors 1 and 2 that is up to the vendor. A receiver of an error 1 cannot trust the apparent OUI/CID in it.
sections.plainLanguage: To return a note you swap the "to" and "from" on the envelope, mark it with the reason, and optionally put it at the back of the queue.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content: IANA allocated 0x008 for the Vendor-Specific RBridge Channel Protocol from the range of RBridge Channel protocols allocated by Standards Action. It also created a subregistry, Vendor RBridge Channel Error Codes, in the TRILL Parameters registry, with Standards Action as the registration procedure. Codes 0x00 to 0x04 are defined as in the previous sections, 0x05 to 0x0F are unassigned, 0x10 to 0xFE are reserved for vendor use and 0xFF is reserved.
sections.plainLanguage: The official list keeps a number for this mailroom and a table of what each error number means, with a block of numbers set aside for companies.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
General TRILL security considerations are in RFC 6325 and general RBridge Channel considerations are in RFC 7178. Neither the Vendor-Specific RBridge Channel Protocol nor the basic RBridge Channel Protocol provides any security assurances or features. The basic channel's first use was as an envelope for BFD messages, which provide their own security.

Any needed security can be provided by fields or processing within the Vendor-Protocol-Specific Data, which is outside the scope of this document. Alternatively or in addition, a Vendor Channel MAY be nested inside the RBridge Channel Header Extension Protocol of RFC 7978, which can provide some security services.
sections.plainLanguage: The mailroom does not lock your notes. If a note is secret, the company has to lock it itself.

fields.name: Zero
fields.desc: Fixed zero value in the header.

fields.name: Flags
fields.desc: Channel header flags, such as SL, defined in RFC 7178.

fields.name: ERR
fields.desc: General channel error field; zero for packets reaching the Vendor Channel.

fields.name: Vendor ID
fields.desc: OUI or CID of the vendor that specifies the message use.

fields.name: VERR
fields.desc: Vendor Channel Error; zero unless reporting an error.

items.label: Message too short
items.desc: Fewer than 4 bytes of channel-specific data.
